name: ATF_TC_CLEANUP(mlock_err, tc)
prose: ATF cleanup routine for mlock_err, compiled only on FreeBSD (inside #ifdef __FreeBSD__): it calls restore_vm_max_wired(), which is declared at the top of the file and defined elsewhere (not read), to undo the set_vm_max_wired(INT_MAX) done by the test body. It has no return value. On other systems the test has no cleanup routine.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(mmap_truncate, tc)
prose: ATF test body checking that ftruncate works while a file is mapped. It opens (creating if needed, mode 0700) the file named by the static `path`; if the open fails the body returns silently without failing. Otherwise it requires (fatal) ftruncate(fd, page) == 0, maps one page of the file read-write and private (requiring MAP_FAILED not returned), writes 'x' to each byte of the page, then requires six more ftruncate calls, with sizes 0, page/8, page/4, page/2, page/12 and page/64, to succeed (seven ftruncate calls in total), unmaps (result ignored) and requires close(fd) == 0. The cleanup routine unlinks the file.
note: contrib/netbsd-tests/lib/libc/sys/t_mmap.c:429-462 (ftruncate calls :444, :453-458; cleanup :464-467). Reviewer (r15) RIGHT: seven ftruncate calls in total (one before the mapping, six after).

name: ATF_TC_BODY(msgrcv_nonblock, tc)
prose: ATF test body for msgrcv with IPC_NOWAIT (timeout 10 s). It creates a System V message queue with key 1234 (IPC_CREAT, mode 0600; ATF_REQUIRE id != -1), sends 10 identical messages of type 0x41 with IPC_NOWAIT (each ATF_REQUIRE success), and forks. The child receives 10 messages of that type with IPC_NOWAIT and _exit(EXIT_FAILURE) as soon as a msgrcv returns -1, else _exit(EXIT_SUCCESS). The parent waits (result ignored) and calls atf_tc_fail if the child was killed by a signal (or WTERMSIG equals SIGKILL), meaning msgrcv blocked, and calls atf_tc_fail 'msgrcv(2) failed' only if WIFEXITED(sta) == 0 and WEXITSTATUS(sta) != EXIT_SUCCESS; since that condition requires the child not to have exited normally, a child that exited normally with EXIT_FAILURE does not fail the test. Finally it requires msgctl(id, IPC_RMID, 0) == 0. The cleanup routine removes the queue if it exists.
note: contrib/netbsd-tests/lib/libc/sys/t_msgrcv.c:245-287 (cleanup :289-292, clean() :64-71). Reviewer (r15) RIGHT: a non-zero normal exit of the child is not detected (:283).

name: ATF_TC_BODY(t_tls_static, tc)
prose: ATF test body for thread-local variables in static binaries. If __HAVE_NO___THREAD is defined it calls atf_tc_skip, which does not return, so the rest is not executed. Otherwise it calls testf(NULL) in the main thread and then twice creates a thread running testf and joins it (the pthread_create results are not checked). testf checks (ATF_CHECK_EQ, non-fatal) that the thread-local var1 is 1 and var2 is 0, calls the external helper testf_helper(), and then checks both are -1. Each new thread starts from the initial values, so every run begins with var1 == 1 and var2 == 0.
note: contrib/netbsd-tests/lib/libc/tls/t_tls_static.c:61-88. Reviewer (r17) RIGHT: atf_tc_skip does not return so testf is not run after it.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(asinf_inrange, tc)
prose: ATF test body comparing asinf with reference values. For each of the eight table entries (x = -1, -0.9, -0.5, -0.1, 0.1, 0.5, 0.9, 1 with their double results, converted to float) it computes whether |(asinf(x) - y) / y| <= FLT_EPSILON and, if not, calls atf_tc_fail_nonfatal with the values and the error in ulp; the loop continues, so every failing entry is reported, not just the first. On NetBSD, for |x| == 0.5 it first calls atf_tc_expect_fail (known ~2 ulp error); on every platform, after the check for |x| == 0.5, it calls atf_tc_expect_pass(), which resets the expectation. So for the +-0.5 entries these ATF expectation calls are made even when no entry fails, and atf_tc_expect_pass() is also called on non-NetBSD systems.
note: contrib/netbsd-tests/lib/libm/t_asin.c:233-255 (table :36-48). Reviewers RIGHT: loop continues after a failure and atf_tc_expect_pass() also runs on non-NetBSD (:252-253).

name: ATF_TC_BODY(asinf_zero_neg, tc)
prose: ATF test body checking asinf(-0.0) == -0.0. It computes y = asinf(-0.0f) and calls atf_tc_fail_nonfatal("asinf(-0.0) != -0.0") if fabsf(y) > 0.0 or the sign bit of y is clear, so only a negative zero passes; a NaN result passes the magnitude test but fails only through the sign-bit test if its sign is clear.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(asinf_zero_pos, tc)
prose: ATF test body checking asinf(+0.0) == +0.0. It computes y = asinf(0.0f) and calls atf_tc_fail_nonfatal("asinf(+0.0) != +0.0") if fabsf(y) > 0.0 or the sign bit of y is set, so only a positive zero passes (a NaN with clear sign bit would also pass).

name: ATF_TC_BODY(casinh, tc)
prose: ATF test body for casinh special values. For each entry of the table (ten entries when __HAVE_NANF is defined, otherwise the first four) of cases of input real/imaginary and expected real/imaginary parts (including infinities and NaNs) it builds the input and expected complex numbers and uses ATF_COMPLEX_EQUAL, which computes casinh(input) and checks with ATF_CHECK_MSG (non-fatal) that the real and imaginary parts are each crudely equal to the expected ones: equal as doubles (so -0 equals +0) or both NaN (only when __HAVE_NANF is defined). Mismatches print the input, result and expectation.
note: contrib/netbsd-tests/lib/libm/t_casinh.c:61-73 (table :11-28, macros :38-52). The table has four unconditional entries and six more under __HAVE_NANF.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(replace, tc)
prose: ATF test body for ppath_replace_idx and ppath_replace_key. After checking that no paths or components are extant (non-fatal checks), it creates an empty path p and checks (ATF_CHECK_EQ) that replacing an index or a key on the empty path returns NULL. It then pushes PPATH_MAX_COMPONENTS index components 0.. into p (checking each push returns p), copies p to cp, pops the last component of cp and pushes the key "key" onto it, and replaces the last component of p with index 0 (return value ignored). It checks that p's last component has index 0 and its other components have indices 0..MAX-2, that cp's first MAX-1 components have indices 0..MAX-2, and that cp's last component is the key "key" (this last check uses atf_tc_fail, fatal). Both paths are released and it checks no paths or components remain extant. Failed ppath_create/ppath_push/prop internalize calls use atf_tc_fail (fatal); the value comparisons use ATF_CHECK_EQ/ATF_CHECK_STREQ, which are non-fatal and only record a failure. Creation or component lookup failures call atf_tc_fail.
note: contrib/netbsd-tests/lib/libppath/t_ppath.c:344-412. Reviewer (r17) RIGHT: index mismatches use ATF_CHECK_EQ (non-fatal), only creation failures and the key check use atf_tc_fail.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(copyset_object_twice_success, tc)
prose: ATF test body for two back-to-back ppath_copyset_* calls. It internalizes the personnel dictionary d, copies it to od, and calls atf_tc_fail if they differ at the start (fatal). It builds three paths: p = John Doe / u.s. citizen, p2 = John Doe / children / [0], p3 = John Doe. It checks (non-fatal) that ppath_get_bool(d, p) is 0 with value true and ppath_get_string(d, p2) is 0 with "Jane Doe". It calls ppath_copyset_bool(d, &nd, p, false) to create the new dictionary nd and records the John Doe object r from nd; then ppath_copyset_string(d, &nd, p2, "Martha Doe") and checks that nd is the same dictionary pointer (the second call modifies the existing copy) and that the John Doe object is the same pointer r. It checks nd has u.s. citizen false and child 0 "Martha Doe". It then uses atf_tc_fail if the original d differs from od, or nd equals od; applies the same two changes directly to od with ppath_set_bool/ppath_set_string and calls atf_tc_fail if od then differs from nd. Finally it releases the paths and dictionaries and checks nothing is extant. Failed ppath_create/ppath_push/prop internalize calls use atf_tc_fail (fatal); the value comparisons use ATF_CHECK_EQ/ATF_CHECK_STREQ, which are non-fatal and only record a failure.
note: contrib/netbsd-tests/lib/libppath/t_ppath.c:426-551. Reviewer (r17) RIGHT: most checks are ATF_CHECK_EQ/STREQ (non-fatal), not atf_tc_fail.

It internalizes the personnel dictionary d and its copy od (fatal if they differ), builds p = John Doe / u.s. citizen, p2 = John Doe / children / [0] and p3 = John Doe, and checks the original values (true and "Jane Doe"). It calls ppath_copydel_bool(d, &nd, p), records the John Doe object r in nd, then ppath_copydel_string(d, &nd, p2), checking nd is the same pointer and r is unchanged. It checks that ppath_get_bool(nd, p) now returns ENOENT and leaves v true. It calls atf_tc_fail if d differs from od or nd equals od; applies ppath_delete_bool and ppath_delete_string to od and calls atf_tc_fail if od then differs from nd. It releases everything and checks nothing is extant. Failed ppath_create/ppath_push/prop internalize calls use atf_tc_fail (fatal); the value comparisons use ATF_CHECK_EQ/ATF_CHECK_STREQ, which are non-fatal and only record a failure.
note: contrib/netbsd-tests/lib/libppath/t_ppath.c:565-685. Reviewer (r15) RIGHT: ATF_CHECK failures are non-fatal; atf_tc_fail is used only for the dictionary comparisons and setup failures.

name: signal_wait_race_threadfunc
prose: Thread function of the signal_wait_race test (the argument is unused). It locks static_mutex (PTHREAD_REQUIRE, fatal on failure). While the shared count is positive it decrements count, increments total, sets toggle = 0, signals static_cond, and waits on static_cond (releasing static_mutex) until toggle == 1; when the loop ends it unlocks static_mutex and returns NULL. So it returns with the mutex unlocked, and if the loop ran at least once toggle is 1 at return (the wait loop only ends when it is 1), not reset to 0.
note: contrib/netbsd-tests/lib/libpthread/t_cond.c:231-251. Reviewers RIGHT: toggle is left at 1 after the final wait (original, :245) and the mutex is unlocked before returning (r15, :248).

name: bar
prose: Thread function of the pthread FPU test (argument unused). It computes d = mul3(mul3(2,3,5), mul3(7,11,13), mul3(17,19,23)) (mul3 yields x*y*z after a sched_yield that must succeed), and requires (fatal) that d == 223092870.0. It then increments the shared recursion_depth under recursion_depth_lock (taking the old value rc). If rc < N_RECURSE (10) it calls recurse(), which creates another thread running bar and sleeps 20 seconds; otherwise it calls atf_tc_pass(), which ends the test and does not return. Only after recurse() returns (after the sleep) does it return NULL; in the pass branch it does not return.
note: contrib/netbsd-tests/lib/libpthread/t_fpu.c:96-116 (mul3 :87-94, recurse :118-123). Reviewers RIGHT: bar returns NULL after recurse() returns (original), atf_tc_pass does not return and mul3's value is asserted (r15).

name: ATF_TC_BODY(pthread_join, tc)
prose: ATF test body that creates one thread running threadfunc1 and joins it (both with PTHREAD_REQUIRE, fatal on failure); the actual checks are in the thread functions. threadfunc1 requires that joining itself fails with EDEADLK, then, in 25 iterations with stack size 65536 * (i + 1), creates a threadfunc2 thread, joins it requiring the returned value i + 1 and that the thread recorded success, requires that joining again fails with ESRCH and that detaching the exited thread fails, destroys the attribute object and calls pthread_exit(NULL). threadfunc2 requires its own stack size to match, increments a static counter and exits with its value.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(siglongjmp1, tc)
prose: ATF test body named for siglongjmp out of a signal handler, but nothing in it raises SIGSEGV, so the handler and the siglongjmp are not executed. It disables core dumps (setrlimit RLIMIT_CORE to 0, result ignored), creates a thread running an empty function (never joined), blocks SIGUSR1 with pthread_sigmask(SIG_SETMASK), installs the handler for SIGSEGV with SIGUSR2 in sa_mask and no flags, and requires sigsetjmp(env, 1) == 0 (true on the direct call). It then reads the signal mask and requires that SIGSEGV and SIGUSR2 are not members and SIGUSR1 is a member; the checks are fatal.
note: contrib/netbsd-tests/lib/libpthread/t_siglongjmp.c:73-102. Reviewer (original) RIGHT: no SIGSEGV is raised.
